about: Spec v0.6: a fixed set of searches over a small wiki shaped like a real brain's, with the first results each must give when search ranks by BM25. Words that are everywhere (brain, wiki, graph, page) and words that are rare (louvain, rrf, bm25, totp) on purpose.

pages.title: What the brain is
pages.body: A brain keeps a journal agents write freely and a wiki people approve. The brain answers over MCP and HTTP. Every brain has members: curators, contributors and readers. The brain never runs a model of its own.

pages.title: The journal
pages.body: Agents save entries to the journal of a brain: decisions, learnings, attempts, facts. The journal is searched with the wiki. A brain journal entry can be forgotten or purged.

pages.title: Proposals
pages.body: The wiki changes through proposals an agent sends and a curator approves in the web. A proposal carries operations: create, edit, move, link, status, merge and revert. The wiki keeps every revision.

pages.title: Wiki health
pages.summary: What needs care in the wiki.
pages.body: The wiki checks itself: orphan pages, broken links, open contradictions, stale pages, long pages and titles almost the same. The health of the wiki is shown in the web for every brain.

pages.title: The graph of the wiki
pages.body: The graph of the wiki draws every page as a node and every link as an edge. The graph moves; the graph can be filtered; the graph shows the page you open. Graph nodes are coloured by their community, found with Louvain over the links.

pages.title: Graph layout
pages.body: The graph layout places graph nodes with forces. Graph edges pull, graph nodes push, the graph settles. A big graph is drawn in a worker so the graph never blocks the page. Graph labels show when the graph is zoomed.

pages.title: How search works
pages.body: Search finds entries and pages together, by any of the words, by quoted phrases and without excluded words, in Spanish and English forms and without accents. With pg_search it ranks by BM25. Meaning search is optional.

pages.title: Meaning search
pages.body: When the administration turns it on, texts are sent to a provider and stored as vectors. Words and meaning are mixed by reciprocal rank fusion, RRF, so a result found both ways comes first.

pages.title: The order of results
pages.body: Results within fifteen percent share a band; inside a band a current page goes first, then the newest. A superseded page never goes before the page that replaced it.

pages.title: Personal tokens
pages.summary: Keys people make for their agents.
pages.body: A person makes a token in the profile for an agent: its brains, read or read and write, and how long it lasts. The token is shown once. A curator can let a token write to the wiki directly.

pages.title: Second factor
pages.summary: TOTP for people who sign in.
pages.body: People who sign in to the web can add a second factor: a TOTP code from an authenticator app, with recovery codes. The key of the second factor is shown in groups of four.

pages.title: Backups
pages.summary: The daily copy and restoring it.
pages.body: rsc-brain makes a daily copy of the database and keeps fourteen. A copy restores into a new installation. A copy made with pg_dump restores with pg_restore too.

pages.title: Updates
pages.body: The administration updates rsc-brain from the web to a published version, with a way back if the update fails. Writes wait during maintenance; reads keep working.

pages.title: Graph ideas
pages.summary: Things to try on the graph.
pages.body: Ideas for the graph: a graph minimap, graph search, graph clusters, a graph timeline. Maybe a graph of the journal too.

pages.title: Brain names
pages.body: A brain name is a slug: lowercase words joined by hyphens. The brain name appears in every address of the brain.
